payload.task_text:
You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

Collect the paper corpus for a literature review. Required exact workflow: (1) call scholarly MCP search-arxiv separately for keyword "transformer" and keyword "attention mechanism"; union and deduplicate results by arXiv-style paper ID, preserving title, authors, publication year, journal reference if present, abstract, and which scholarly query matched. Retrieve every result those two calls return. (2) call arxiv_local search_papers separately for query "transformer" and query "neural network", use broad relevant NLP/ML categories and max_results=50 each; union and deduplicate by paper ID. Download each unique arxiv_local paper and read enough to capture its abstract, title, authors, year, and journal reference if present. (3) Return a compact but complete JSON-like structured list for each source and an overlap list by exact normalized paper ID. Do not modify files or external systems. Scope is only collection and read-only extraction. Acceptance: two distinct searches per source are evidenced, no duplicate IDs within each source, and every returned record has ID/title/authors/year/abstract (journal reference nullable).
Collect transformer papers

The main agent successfully downloaded all nine arxiv_local IDs: 2009.06732, 1706.03762, 1810.04805, 2005.14165, 1910.10683, 1207.00580, 1502.03167, 1409.0473, 1312.06199. Now call arxiv_local read_paper for each and verify/correct title, author list, year, journal reference, and abstract. Return only corrections versus your prior corpus plus confirmation that every abstract was read. Do not modify anything.
Read downloaded abstracts

Create the local analysis deliverables in the only allowed workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace. Read review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md there. Use this deduplicated corpus (Scholarly IDs: 2009.06732,1706.03762,1810.04805,2005.14165,1910.10683,1409.0473; Arxiv IDs: those six plus 1207.00580,1502.03167,1312.06199). Records:
2009.06732 | Efficient Transformers: A Survey | Yi Tay; Mostafa Dehghani; Dara Bahri | 2020 | ACM Computing Surveys 2022 | Transformer model architectures have driven NLP advances; a comprehensive survey of efficient transformer architectures reducing computational and memory complexity.
1706.03762 | Attention Is All You Need | Ashish Vaswani; Noam Shazeer; Niki Parmar | 2017 | NeurIPS 2017 | Proposes the Transformer, a simple sequence architecture based solely on attention, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions.
1810.04805 | BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding | Jacob Devlin; Ming-Wei Chang; Kenton Lee | 2018 | NAACL 2019 | Introduces BERT, pre-training deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text and fine-tuning them for many tasks.
2005.14165 | Language Models are Few-Shot Learners | Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Mann; Nick Ryder | 2020 | NeurIPS 2020 | Presents GPT-3, a large Transformer language model whose scaling improves task-agnostic few-shot performance.
1910.10683 | Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer | Colin Raffel; Noam Shazeer; Adam Roberts | 2019 | JMLR 2020 | Introduces T5, a unified text-to-text transfer-learning framework for text-based language problems.
1409.0473 | Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate | Dzmitry Bahdanau; Kyunghyun Cho; Yoshua Bengio | 2014 | ICLR 2015 | Applies a learned attention mechanism to neural machine translation to avoid a fixed-length-vector bottleneck.
1207.00580 | Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors | Geoffrey E. Hinton; Nitish Srivastava | 2012 | null | Describes dropout to address overfitting in neural networks.
1502.03167 | Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training | Sergey Ioffe; Christian Szegedy | 2015 | null | Proposes batch normalization to stabilize changing layer-input distributions and accelerate deep network training.
1312.06199 | Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning | Volodymyr Mnih; Koray Kavukcuoglu | 2013 | null | Applies a deep neural network with reinforcement learning to learn control policies from high-dimensional sensory input.
Sources: first six are Both; last three Arxiv only. Build and RUN a Python script named analyze_papers.py that stores collected data, assigns exactly one methodology category by keyword rules from guidelines (use clear deterministic priority such as Survey, Applications, Training Methods, Architecture Design, with sensible fallback), performs exact normalized-ID overlap, and writes analysis_results.json including records and category summaries. Then create Transformer_Literature_Review.docx (minimum 500 words) with exact requested title, Introduction, one section per category, each paper title/authors/year/brief abstract-based description, mark overlap papers, discuss year trends, and conclude with field state/research gaps. Create Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx with exactly sheets Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix and requested literal columns/values; IDs must be plain text, no formulas. Apply readable professional formatting. Verify script ran, JSON is valid, docx exists and >=500 words, workbook sheet names/data/formula absence. Return artifact paths, final categorized record list, and verification evidence.
Build analysis artifacts

Create the required Notion knowledge base. There are currently no accessible pages (a search returned zero), so first create a workspace-level parent page titled "Transformer NLP Literature Review Workspace", then create a database beneath it titled exactly "Research Paper Tracker". Database properties exactly: Title (title), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Create exactly one database entry for each of these nine records:
1) 2009.06732 | Efficient Transformers: A Survey | Yi Tay; Mostafa Dehghani; Dara Bahri | 2020 | Survey | Both | Transformer model architectures have driven NLP advances; a comprehensive survey of efficient transformer architectures reducing computational and memory complexity.
2) 1706.03762 | Attention Is All You Need | Ashish Vaswani; Noam Shazeer; Niki Parmar | 2017 | Architecture Design | Both | Proposes the Transformer, a simple sequence architecture based solely on attention, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions.
3) 1810.04805 | BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding | Jacob Devlin; Ming-Wei Chang; Kenton Lee | 2018 | Training Methods | Both | Introduces BERT, pre-training deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text and fine-tuning them for many tasks.
4) 2005.14165 | Language Models are Few-Shot Learners | Tom B. Brown; Benjamin Mann; Nick Ryder | 2020 | Applications | Both | Presents GPT-3, a large Transformer language model whose scaling improves task-agnostic few-shot performance.
5) 1910.10683 | Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer | Colin Raffel; Noam Shazeer; Adam Roberts | 2019 | Training Methods | Both | Introduces T5, a unified text-to-text transfer-learning framework for text-based language problems.
6) 1409.0473 | Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate | Dzmitry Bahdanau; Kyunghyun Cho; Yoshua Bengio | 2014 | Applications | Both | Applies a learned attention mechanism to neural machine translation to avoid a fixed-length-vector bottleneck.
7) 1207.00580 | Improving Neural Networks by Preventing Co-adaptation of Feature Detectors | Geoffrey E. Hinton; Nitish Srivastava | 2012 | Training Methods | Arxiv | Describes dropout to address overfitting in neural networks.
8) 1502.03167 | Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training | Sergey Ioffe; Christian Szegedy | 2015 | Training Methods | Arxiv | Proposes batch normalization to stabilize changing layer-input distributions and accelerate deep network training.
9) 1312.06199 | Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning | Volodymyr Mnih; Koray Kavukcuoglu | 2013 | Training Methods | Arxiv | Applies a deep neural network with reinforcement learning to learn control policies from high-dimensional sensory input.
Important: Source schema option must be exactly "Arxiv" rather than "Arxiv only" per user request. Verify by querying the database, confirming 9 entries and all properties populated. Return parent page ID, database ID, and verification count. Do not touch local files.
Create Notion tracker

Verification found the Excel workbook does NOT match the user’s exact requested schemas. Correct Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in place and verify it. Required exact sheet layouts, with no extra columns:
Paper_Catalog columns exactly: Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source, Category. Use Source literal values only Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both; the three non-overlap papers must say Arxiv (not Arxiv only).
Method_Comparison columns exactly: Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, Key_Papers. Compute Avg_Year as literal values (no formulas): Survey 2020; Applications 2017; Training Methods 2015.4; Architecture Design 2017. Key_Papers must list titles (not IDs), ideally all titles in that category.
Citation_Matrix columns exactly: Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly, In_Arxiv, Overlap. For six overlap IDs use Yes/Yes/Yes; for IDs 1207.00580,1502.03167,1312.06199 use No/Yes/No.
All IDs plain text, all values literal, no formulas. Preserve exactly three sheet names. Apply readable formatting. Verify by readback and report exact used ranges, headers, 9 data rows where applicable, and no formulas. Do not alter Word/JSON/script.
